A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MAviS research work. All 27 pages in each version, including figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison after matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAviS-Bench evaluations, real-world video results, and training ablations in Tables 1–4, with additional lexical results in Appendix C, Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark evaluations, video results, and ablations, including Appendix C's results.

M1.justification: The annotation pipelines, MiniCPM-o-2.6-based MAviS-Chat architecture, LoRA adaptation, and audio–image–audio fine-tuning procedure are unchanged in Sections 3 and 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same avian image, audio, and text coverage, MAviS-Bench tasks, and real-world video evaluation. Appendix E's complete recording-ID sequence is identical.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 1.5, Phi-4-MM-Instruct, and MiniCPM-o-2.6; Table 2 retains GPT-4o-mini as the video comparator. The Gemini citation replacement does not change the evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, benchmark composition, evaluation metrics, video-question protocol, and training configurations are unchanged. This includes the 1,892 audio and 2,017 image evaluation samples and the MAviS-Eval rubric.

E4.justification: The LoRA-layer, training-order, and data-size ablations in Tables 3–4 are identical. Appendix C's lexical comparison and Appendix D's qualitative examples are also retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the accompanying findings are unchanged. For example, MAviS-Chat retains combined MAviS-Eval 59.92 in Table 1 and video MAviS-Eval 39.30 versus GPT-4o-mini's 31.06 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Task definitions and evaluation scoring rules are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset, benchmark, and conversational-model contributions, including claims about domain adaptation and performance relative to open-source baselines.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality grounding, projection-layer tuning, training order, and data size are unchanged. The limitations concerning rare species, environmental noise, data diversity, generalization, and future video fine-tuning are also identical.

D1.justification: Architecture and training details, preprocessing descriptions, appendix prompts, recording identifiers, licensing restrictions, and promised resource access are unchanged. Relocated appendix material supplies no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces the supporting Gemini reference: Thoppilan et al. (2023), 'Gemini: A unified multimodal large language model,' arXiv:2303.06601, becomes Team et al. (2024), 'Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context,' arXiv:2403.05530. This is one reference substitution; related-work discussion and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the Gemini author/year citation, its expanded bibliography entry, and the arXiv version/date stamp. Substantive prose, terminology, section order, and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer bibliography shifts the final reference onto page 12, leaving substantial whitespace and moving Table 5 to the right column. Figure 5 moves from page 12 to 13, and Figures 6–7 move from pages 13–14 to 14–15. Their content and captions are unchanged; the recording list merely reflows.

improvement.justification: The replacement reference explicitly identifies a Gemini 1.5 report, improving attribution and traceability for the retained baseline. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The resulting appendix layout is less compact but preserves all content, so the overall benefit is limited.
